source.title: AICPA 2017 Trust Services Criteria (revised Points of Focus, 2022)
source.wording: Omnisciente summaries; no licensed verbatim reproduction

CC1.1.review_note: Summary uses conduct-related Points of Focus to clarify ethical commitment; it does not prescribe a formal policy.

items.text: Management establishes expectations for ethical behavior and follows through when conduct falls short.
items.source_reference: CC1.1; conduct expectations and follow-through Points of Focus, page 15

items.text: Communicate conduct expectations during onboarding and when responsibilities change.
Provide a reporting route and assign responsibility for consistent follow-up.
Review recurring conduct concerns and whether corrective responses address their causes.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC1.1

CC1.2.review_note: Oversight arrangements depend on entity size and structure; see source footnote 15.

items.text: The governing body provides independent oversight of the development and performance of internal control.
Give the governing body control issues, decisions and unresolved actions in a usable briefing.
Have oversight members evaluate whether their challenge changed management decisions.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC1.2

CC1.3.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: Management establishes structures, reporting lines, authorities and responsibilities, with governing-body oversight, to support the organization's objectives.
Keep reporting lines and delegated decision rights accessible to control owners.
Clarify the handoffs between internal teams and outsourced providers.

CC1.4.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization attracts, develops and retains people with the competence needed to achieve its objectives.
Connect hiring and development activities to the competencies of each control role.
Arrange cover for control responsibilities when key staff are absent.
Evaluate whether training resolves observed execution errors.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC1.4

CC1.5.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization holds individuals accountable for their internal-control responsibilities.
Include control responsibilities in performance conversations and follow up on missed obligations.
Review whether delivery incentives encourage staff to bypass controls.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC1.5

CC2.1.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization obtains or generates and uses relevant, quality information for internal control.
Identify each control owner's information needs and the responsible data source.
Check important reports for missing, outdated or inconsistent information before use.
Reconcile a sample of management reports to their underlying records.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC2.1

CC2.2.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization communicates objectives and internal-control responsibilities to the people who need them.
Use role-specific communications for control changes and escalation routes.
Ask a sample of recipients to demonstrate how they would report a control concern.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC2.2

CC2.3.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization communicates with external parties about matters affecting internal control.
Assign owners for customer and supplier communications about responsibilities and changes.
Route incoming concerns to a responsible team and track the response.

CC3.1.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization states its objectives clearly enough to identify and assess risks to their achievement.
Connect scoped service commitments to clear objectives used in risk assessment.

CC3.2.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization identifies and analyzes risks to its objectives and decides how those risks will be managed.
Record risk analysis, response decisions and accountable owners in the existing risk workflow.
Revisit risk decisions when threat or business assumptions change.
Challenge major risk assumptions using observed incidents and near misses.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC3.2

CC3.3.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization considers the potential for fraud when assessing risks to its objectives.
Include realistic fraud scenarios and relevant participants in risk discussions.

CC3.4.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization identifies and assesses changes that could significantly affect internal control.
Use business, technology and supplier change workflows to trigger risk reassessment.
Compare completed changes with risk reviews to identify missed triggers.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC3.4

CC4.1.review_note: Ongoing or separate evaluation is already part of the criterion, not an optional assurance upgrade.

items.text: The organization performs appropriate ongoing or separate evaluations to determine whether internal control is present and functioning.
Assign evaluation scope, responsibilities and timing based on control risk.
Compare conclusions from different evaluators where results conflict.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC4.1

CC4.2.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: Control deficiencies are evaluated and communicated promptly to those responsible for correction, including appropriate leadership.
Assign remediation owners and track deficiencies through the existing Findings and Actions workflows.
Have someone other than the action owner challenge closure support for significant deficiencies.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC4.2

CC5.1.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization selects and develops control activities that reduce risks to acceptable levels.
Map selected controls to the risks they address and explain any compensating arrangements.

CC5.2.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization establishes general control activities over technology that support its objectives.
Identify technology dependencies and assign ownership of supporting access, change and maintenance controls.

CC5.3.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: Policies establish expectations for control activities.
Procedures put those control expectations into action.
Make procedures accessible to the people performing them and establish how exceptions are handled.
Compare actual execution with the procedure after significant operational changes.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC5.3

CC6.1.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization implements logical-access security over protected information assets to protect them from security events.
Identify protected assets and access paths, then apply authentication and access rules appropriate to their risks.
Include access-control decisions in architecture reviews.
Validate that a sample of disallowed access attempts is blocked across different access paths.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC6.1

CC6.2.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: For access administered by the organization, internal and external users are registered and authorized before credentials or access are issued.
For access administered by the organization, credentials are removed when user access is no longer authorized.
Connect credential approval and removal to joiner, mover and leaver workflows.
Review credentials for accounts without a current owner or business purpose.
Reconcile account records with personnel and supplier records to identify missed removals.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC6.2

CC6.3.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization grants, changes and removes access according to roles, responsibilities and system design, considering least privilege and segregation of duties.
Document role entitlements and approval responsibilities for access changes.
Review privileges and incompatible access when responsibilities change.
Test effective permissions rather than relying only on the requested access list.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC6.3

CC6.4.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization restricts physical access to relevant facilities and protected information assets to authorized personnel.
Assign responsibility for visitor access, badge changes and recovery of physical devices.

CC6.5.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: Protection of physical assets continues until recoverability of their data and software has been reduced and is no longer needed for organizational objectives.
Keep asset protection in place until the disposal or transfer owner confirms the selected sanitization outcome.
Validate sanitization results for a sample of retired assets, including supplier-handled disposal.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC6.5

CC6.6.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization protects against threats from outside its system boundaries through logical-access security measures.
Maintain an approved inventory of external access points and their permitted uses.
Review boundary-rule exceptions with a named owner.
Validate exposed access paths against the approved boundary design.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC6.6

CC6.7.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: Information transmission, movement and removal are restricted to authorized users and processes.
Information is protected during transmission, movement and removal.
Define approved transfer routes and handling rules for sensitive information and removable media.
Test whether an unauthorized transfer attempt is prevented or detected as intended.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC6.7

CC6.8.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization prevents or detects and acts on unauthorized or malicious software.
Restrict software installation and route suspected malicious software to a response owner.
Exercise malware response safely in an isolated test environment.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC6.8

CC7.1.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: Monitoring detects configuration changes that introduce vulnerabilities.
Monitoring identifies exposure to newly discovered vulnerabilities.
Connect configuration and vulnerability monitoring results to prioritized remediation work.
Measure repeat vulnerabilities and verify whether prior fixes remain effective.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC7.1

CC7.2.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: System components and operations are monitored for anomalies associated with malicious activity, natural events or errors affecting objectives.
Anomalies are analyzed to determine whether they are security events.
Assign anomaly triage responsibilities and escalation routes.
Monitor whether collection and alerting tools are themselves working.
Use controlled scenarios to check that important anomalies reach the right responder.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC7.2

CC7.3.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: Security events are evaluated to determine whether they are incidents.
Action is taken to prevent or address failures of the organization's objectives.
Record event classification, impact analysis and the reason for escalation or closure.
Revisit a sample of closed events to challenge missed-incident assumptions.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC7.3

CC7.4.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization executes a defined incident-response program to understand, contain, remediate and communicate identified incidents.
Keep response roles, contacts and communications routes usable during an incident.
Record the sequence of containment and remediation decisions.
Review incident patterns and exercise outcomes to improve response decisions.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC7.4

CC7.5.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization identifies, develops and implements activities to recover from identified security incidents.
Assign recovery activities and validate restored functionality before resuming normal operation.
Review whether incident recovery changes prevent recurrence.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC7.5

CC8.1.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: System changes are authorized, designed, developed or acquired, configured, documented, tested, approved and implemented to support organizational objectives.
Use change records to connect approvals, tests and release decisions.
Define how urgent changes receive appropriate review and follow-up.
Compare deployed changes with approved records to identify untracked releases.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC8.1

CC9.1.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization selects and develops activities to mitigate risks arising from potential business disruptions.
Translate credible disruption scenarios into workable continuity arrangements and responsibilities.
Exercise dependency failures that could defeat the planned alternative processing approach.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC9.1

CC9.2.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization assesses and manages risks associated with vendors and business partners.
Assign vendor-risk owners and connect due diligence, requirements and issue follow-up.
Reassess significant service changes and plan access and data handling at termination.
Challenge concentration risk across critical providers and their dependencies.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for CC9.2

A1.1.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization maintains, monitors and evaluates processing capacity and system-component use so it can respond to capacity demand.
Use demand forecasts and operating thresholds to trigger capacity changes.
Compare forecasts with observed peaks and investigate persistent forecasting errors.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for A1.1

A1.2.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: Environmental protections, software, backups and recovery infrastructure are authorized, designed, developed or acquired, approved, operated, maintained and monitored for availability objectives.
Monitor backup jobs and environmental alerts, with owners for failure follow-up.
Check that backup and recovery arrangements cover the scoped systems and data.
Evaluate whether a shared failure could defeat both primary and recovery infrastructure.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for A1.2

A1.3.review_note: Recovery testing is criterion-derived; schedule, records and extra validation are implementation guidance.

items.text: The organization tests recovery-plan procedures that support system recovery.
Assign a risk-based test schedule and retain recovery results.
Track test failures and resulting recovery-plan changes.
Compare restoration performance across exercises to identify persistent weaknesses.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for A1.3

items.text: Use an independent observer for a significant recovery exercise.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for A1.3

C1.1.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization identifies and maintains confidential information according to its confidentiality objectives.
Define confidential information and connect handling and retention decisions to applicable commitments.

C1.2.review_note: No source gap identified for this criterion summary; control design remains entity-specific.

items.text: The organization disposes of confidential information according to its confidentiality objectives.
Assign disposal responsibility when retention ends, including information held by service providers.
Sample completed disposal records and validate the intended result across relevant storage locations.
items.source_reference: Omnisciente additional assurance guidance for C1.2
